Serial number of the case : 2020/09
Date of the commission of the offence : 03.01.2009
Date of filing of the complaint : 14.12.2009

Name of the Complainant : Sh. Ranjeet Singh, Food Inspector Offence complained of or proved : Section 2 (ix) (k) of PFA Act, 1954   and Rule 32 (e) of PFA Rules 1955, 
 which is punishable us 16 (1) (a) of PFA Act 1954 r/w Section 7 of the   PFA Act.
Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty Final order : Acquitted Arguments heard on : 29.01.2016 Judgment announced on : 29.01.2016.

Brief facts of the case 1.In brief the case of the prosecution is that on 03.01.2009 at about 04.30 p.m., Food Inspector Ranjeet Singh and Field Assistant Sh. Rakesh Kumar, under the supervision and directions of SDM/LHA Sh. A. K Sharma visited the premises of M/s SRS Entertainment Limited, Main Road, Mauj Pur, Delhi110053, where accused Hari Shankar Sharma who was the vendorcummanager was found present conducting the business of sale of various food articles including Masoor Dal, for sale for human consumption and in compliance of the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as the Act & Rules) the Food Inspector collected/ purchased the sample of Masoor Dal.

2.During the course of investigation, it was revealed that Hari Shankar Sharma S/o Sh. Ved Prakash Sharma was the vendorcumManager of M/s SRS Entertainment Limited, 190/5A & 190/5A1 main Road, Mauj Pur, Delhi110053 at the time of taking sample and as such he is incharge of and responsible for the conduct of business of said sales unit of the Company.

The sample article of food "Masoor Dal" was packed by M/s SRS Entertainment Limited at their Packing Unit: SRS Daily bazar, C4/1,
North Chhajju Pur, 100 fit Road, Shahdara, Delhi32 and supplied to the above said sales outlet at 190/5A & 190/AA1 main Road, Maupur, Delhi53.

M/s SRS Entertainment Limited is a company having four Directors ,namely, (1)Sh.
Sunil Jindal S/o Sh. Girraj Singh (2) Sh. Raju Bansal S/o Sh Nanak Chand (3) Sh. Vinod Gupta S/o Sh. Chunni Lal, (4) Sh. Anil Kumar Jindal S/o Sh Girraj Singh Jindal, M/s SRS Entertainment Limited has not appointed the nominee under the provisions of PFA Act/Rules, either for the above said sales outlet or for the packing unit of the company and as such all the above said four directors are responsible for the day to day business of the said company at its above said sales outlet and Packing Unit.
Being a Company, M/s SRS Entertainment Limited is also liable for its sales outlet as Da vs .

Hari Shankar Sharma Page 1/8 on 29 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79720460/
2 well as Packing Unit.
3.It is further the prosecution's case that the sample was sent to Public Analyst for analysis and as per the report of Public Analyst the sample was was misbranded because there is violation of Rule 32 (e) however Masoor Dal conforms to standard on the basis of test performed and accordingly after obtaining the necessary Sanction / Consent under Section 20 of the Act, the present complaint was filed for violation of provisions of Section 2 ((ix) (k) of PFA Act 1954 and Rule 32 (e) of PFA Rules 1955 which is punishable under Section 16 (1) (a) of the PFA Act 1954 r/w Section 7 of the PFA Act 1954.
4.After the complaint was filed, the accused persons i.e Hari Shankar Sharma, Raju Bansal and M/s SRS Entertainment Limited were summoned vide orders dated 14.12.2009.

Accused Sunil Kumar,
Vinod Gupta and Anil Kumar were not summoned.

5.Notice for violation of provision of Section 2 (ix) (k) of PFA Act, 1954 and Rule 32 (e) of PFA Rules 1955, which is punishable us 16 (1) (a) of PFA Act 1954 r/w Section 7 of the PFA Act 1954 were framed against the accused Hari Shankar Sharma, Raju Bansal and M/s SRS Entertainment Ltd,
Sales Outlet: SRS Daily Bazar, 190/5A, 190/5A1, Main Road, Mauj Pur, Delhi, vide order dated 22.03.2010 to which accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
6.Statement of accused Hari Shankar Sharma, Raju Bansal and M/s SRS Entertainment Limited U/s 313 Cr. P.C. were recorded on 30.01.2012 wherein the accused persons claimed themselves to be innocent.
Despite opportunity given to accused persons they did not lead any defence.

A brief scrutiny of the evidence recorded in the matter is as under:
7.PW1 Sh. A. K. Sharma deposed that on 03.01.2009, he was posted as SDM/LHA, Seelampur, New Delhi.

He further deposed that on that day he alongwith FI Ranjeet Singh and FA Rakesh Kumar,
under his supervision and direction visited the premises of M/s SRS Entertainment Ltd., Main Road, Maujpur, Delhi where accused Hari Shankar Sharma, was found conducting the business of food articles stored there for sale for human consumption including Masoor Dal which was lying in sealed packets of 1 kg each.
He further deposed that first of all, they disclosed their identity and intention to purchase a sample of Masoor Dal from the accused/vendor for analysis and he agreed for the same.

He further stated that before starting the sample proceedings, FI requested some customers present in the store as well as some passerby to join in the sample proceedings but none came forward then on the request of FI Sh.Ranjeet Singh, FA Sh.Rakesh Kumar joined as a witness in sample proceedings.

He further deposed that thereafter at about 4.30 PM, FI purchased from the vendor 3 sealed packets of 1 Kg each of Masoor Dal bearing identical label declaration, which was reproduced on notice in form VI.
He further stated that the so purchased quantity of sample commodity was divided by the FI then and there into three equal parts by putting one originally sealed packet as one counterpart.

He further deposed that all the three counterparts were separately packed and sealed and LHA slips, bearing his code number and signatures were affixed on all the three counterparts and vendor's signatures were obtained on each counterpart in such manner so as to appear partly on LHA slip and partly on the wrapper of the counterpart.

He further deposed that Da vs . Hari Shankar Sharma Page 1/8 on 29 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79720460/
3 the price of the sample commodity i.e.Rs.199/ was paid vide vendor's receipt Ex.PW1/A bearing the signatures of the vendor at point A.

He further stated that notice in form VI vide Ex.PW1/B bearing the signatures of vendor at point A was prepared and the vendor made an endorsement on the same at portion X to X to the effect that the sample commodity was packed by them and was endorsement at portion Y to Y.
He also deposed that the Panchnama Ex.PW1/C was also prepared.
He further stated that notice under Section 14A of the Act of 1954 was also prepared addressing to M/s S.R.S. Entertainment Ltd. vide Ex.PW1/D bearing the signatures of vendor at point A.

He also deposed that the report under Rule 9(e) of PFA Rules was also prepared at the spot vide Ex.PW1/E bearing his signatures at point A, signatures of witness at point B and signatures of FI at point C.
He further stated that the vendor also issued a cash receipt towards the price of sample commodity Ex.PW1/A1 bearing his signatures at point A.
All the documents Ex.PW1/A to Ex.PW1/D were read over and explained to the accused in Hindi and he signed at point A, witness signed at point B and FI signed at point C.

He further deposed that two counterparts of the sample alongwith two copies of memo in form VII were deposited with him on 05.01.2009 i.e on the next working day in sealed condition vide LHA Receipt Ex. PW1/F bearing his signatures at point A and signatures of FI at point A, under intimation that one counterpart of the same has already been deposited with PA.

He deposed that PA Report was received which is Ex. PW1/G, bearing signatures of PA at point A,
which revealed that sample was misbranded.

Accordingly, on his directions FI Sh. Ranjeet Singh conducted the investigation and put the entire case file before him and he forwarded the same to Sh.
D. P. Dwivedi, the then Director, PFA, who after going through the same gave his consent for prosecution, which is Ex. PW1/H, bearing signatures of the said Director at point A.

He deposed that thereafter, complaint was filed in the Court by Sh. Ranjeet Singh, FI, which is Ex. PW1/I, bearing his signatures at point A and then intimation letter along with copy of PA Report were sent to accused persons through registered post, which were not received back undelivered.

He deposed that however corrigendum regarding the intimation letter the sample commodity was mentioned as Ghee, but in fact it was Masoor Dal, the same as also served by hand upon vendor for all the accused persons.
He deposed that intimation letter Ex. PW1/J bearing his signatures at point A and the endorsement of the vendor regarding receiving of intimation letter is at portion X to X.

The corrigendum in this regard is Ex. PW1/K, bearing his signatures at point A.
8.During his cross examination
, he stated that it is not in his knowledge that whether any other case prior to the present case regarding the violation of Rule 32 (e) of PFA Rules was also initiated against the accused persons.
He stated that he cannot say whether the present case is the first violation under Rule 32 (e).
He admitted that earlier there was a policy of the department to issue warning in respect of first violation under Rule 32 of PFA Rules.
9.PW2 Sh. Ranjeet Singh, Food Inspector deposed on the same lines as deposed by PW 1 and PW2 in their examination in chief.
10.This so far is the evidence in the matter.
11.It is argued by Ld. SPP for complainant that there is sufficient evidence to return the finding of guilt against the accused persons.
On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the accused has stated that the Da vs . Hari Shankar Sharma Page 1/8 on 29 January, 2016

4
Hon'ble Supreme Court vide judgment of Dwarka Nath & Anr. Vs. MCD AIR 1971 SC 1844 held the Rule 32(e) of PFA Rules, 155 to be ultra vires.

entities.text: Dwarka Nath & Anr. Vs. MCD AIR 1971 SC 1844
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, it was the first violation of the accused of label condition provided under Rule 32 of PFA Rules and as per the policy no. policy no. F6 (228)/85/ENF/PFA, he is entitled to written warning.
So, the prosecution was not correctly launched against the accused.
12.I have heard the arguments advanced at bar by Ld. defence counsel as also the Ld. SPP for complainant.
I have also carefully gone through the entire record of the case including evidence recorded in the present case.
13.The accused is not entitled to benefit of policy no. F6 (228)/85/ENF/PFA of Food Department as the said policy was withdrawn vide Order No. 5/07dated 14.09.2007.
The sample in the present case was lifted on 03.01.2009.

So, the said policy was not in force at the time of lifting of sample in the present case.
14.The Hon'ble Supreme Court vide judgment of Dwarka Nath (supra) held Rule 32(e) of PFA Rules requiring batch number or code number on label of containers to be ultra vires the rule making power of the Central Government U/Sec. 23 of PFA Act
and declared it to be invalid.
The said judgment was further followed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in judgment NCT of Delhi Vs. Mohinder Singh Criminal Appeal No. 1470/2011 SC decided on 27.08.2015.

entities.text: NCT of Delhi Vs. Mohinder Singh Criminal Appeal No. 1470/2011 SC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So, the accused was not obliged to mention the Batch Number or Code Number on label of container/s on account of the aforesaid judgment.

In view of the same, the accused Hari Shankar Sharma, Raju Bansal and M /s SRS Entertainment are acquitted for violation of Rule 32(e) of PFA Rules 1955 which is punishable u/s 16(1) (a) read with Section 7 of the PFA Act.

Announced in the open Court (PRIYA MAHENDRA)
on 29.01.2016.
